title: CATL sodium-ion batteries
summary: Sodium-ion cells aimed at cold climates and cost-sensitive vehicles.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

CATL launched a sodium-ion product line in 2025, claiming around 175 Wh/kg and usable range in cold conditions where lithium-ion loses capacity. Sodium is abundant and avoids lithium and cobalt price risk, but lower energy density means the cells suit small cars and stationary storage before long-range vehicles. Commercial scale depends on cathode and hard-carbon supply chains.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Pilot
Estimated window 2025–2028
Confidence label Researching
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

Investment Exposure

Sodium-ion matters most where lithium price spikes or cold weather dominate; it is a complement, not a replacement.

What Would Change The View

  • Mass-production timing and cost per kWh.
  • Cycle life in real storage duty.
  • Hard-carbon anode supply.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
